imageAlt: Students crowd around an outdoor table building marshmallow structures at Science Odyssey.

description:
At this year’s Science Odyssey, Pillars of Tech hosted an interactive engineering booth designed to introduce participants to the concepts of structural strength and material efficiency.

Students took part in a marshmallow structural challenge, where they were given materials to design and build a structure capable of supporting as many pennies as possible. The activity encouraged participants to think like engineers, balancing strength, stability, and efficiency.

Once the structures were built, we tested them by gradually adding pennies to measure how much weight they could support. Participants quickly learned that the strongest structure wasn’t always the one that used the most materials. In engineering, efficiency matters just as much as strength; a design that holds significant weight while using fewer materials is often the most impressive.

The challenge sparked creativity, problem-solving, and collaboration among students of all ages. One standout design successfully supported 85 pennies, the highest weight achieved during the event.

Through activities like this, Pillars of Tech aims to make STEM concepts tangible, engaging, and fun, helping inspire the next generation of engineers and innovators.

description:
Wildcat Tank brought Altamont students together for an evening of creativity, entrepreneurship, and confident public speaking. Inspired by "Shark Tank," students developed original STEM-based product ideas and presented them to a panel of guest judges, explaining their designs, features, and real-world purpose.

The event highlighted impressive innovation, problem-solving, and presentation skills from every participant. Families, judges, and supporters helped create an encouraging, high-energy atmosphere that made the night a memorable celebration of student ideas.

description:
At Family Science Night at Altamont Creek Elementary School, students explored student-built VEX robots from Livermore High School’s Green Engineering Academy (GEA).

Students put the robots to the test by driving through a maze, collecting cubes, and completing a precision “narrow path” challenge to transport blocks across the table. These hands-on activities helped students explore how robots work—from coding and motors to wiring and control systems.

We’re grateful to the Green Engineering Academy for sharing their incredible robots and helping us bring a memorable robotics experience to families.

What is the GEA?

The Green Engineering Academy is a four-year engineering pathway at Livermore High School (founded in 2010) that combines rigorous academics with hands-on, industry-relevant engineering experiences. The program follows the Project Lead the Way (PLTW) curriculum and gives students experience with tools like Onshape, Fusion 360, and Revit—preparing them for college engineering programs, apprenticeships, and technical careers through real-world projects and applied engineering experiences.

title: Career Panel
imageAlt: Career Panel speakers and student organizers pose for a group photo on stage.
heroImageAlt: Career Panel speakers and student organizers pose for a group photo on stage.
description:
What does a career in STEM actually look like? At Granada High School, Pillars of Tech brought students and STEM professionals together for an evening of honest advice, career stories, and conversations about where a curiosity for science can lead.

The first panel featured Matthew Johnson, Anna Winter, Mark Dedon, Randy Simpson, and Joel Bowers. They shared perspectives on field research, working through setbacks in the lab, and opportunities across earth science, atmospheric research, conservation, climate technology, and national security. The discussion gave students a closer look at both the exciting discoveries and the persistence behind scientific work.

Amy Aines, Yolanda Fintschenko, Roger Aines, and Russ Walsh joined the second panel to talk about building a future in STEM. Topics included bringing research into the real world, communicating ideas through storytelling, standing out early in a career, and finding mentors along the way.

An open Q&A gave attendees space to ask their own questions, and the conversations continued afterward as students connected with panelists one-on-one. Thank you to all nine speakers, our partners at Livermore and Granada HOSA, and everyone who joined us for an evening of exploring possibilities and making connections.

title: STEM Into the Night
location: Junction Avenue K-8 School, 298 Junction Ave, Livermore, CA 94551
registrationNote: Registration is for Junction students only. The registration link will be shared through the school.
description:
Pillars of Tech hosted STEM Into the Night in partnership with the Junction Avenue K-8 STEM class, bringing students and community partners together for an evening of hands-on STEM exploration.

Students explored engineering and creative problem-solving through an index card boat activity, a robot hand activity, pixel graphing, and an index card tower challenge. Rocket launchers and a physics activity added more opportunities to explore science in action.

Health and science activities included CPR training, building a model heart, and learning how to use a stethoscope.

Thank you to the Junction STEM class and our community partners, including the Green Engineering Academy from Livermore High School and Diabetes Smart, for helping bring the evening to life.

Learn more about the Green Engineering Academy at www.livermoregea.org and Diabetes Smart at diabetessmart.org.

title: Altamont Creek Elementary Open House
description:
The Altamont Creek Open House brought our students together for an exciting day of hands-on exploration and scientific discovery! Designed to spark curiosity and a love for STEM, the interactive activity gave students a front-row seat to the wonders of physics and engineering.

The event featured one major highlight that captured the imagination of our young scientists:

• DIY Paper Helicopters: A crowd-favorite build-and-fly activity where students crafted their own spinning helicopters from a simple strip of paper and a paperclip. By folding, adjusting, and launching their creations, they explored the concepts of aerodynamics, drag, and gravity — discovering firsthand how angled blades interact with air to create lift and rotation, just like a real helicopter.

The event highlighted impressive curiosity, critical thinking, and a joy for learning from every participant. Thank you to the families, volunteers, and supporters who helped create an encouraging, high-energy atmosphere that made the day a memorable celebration of student discovery!

description:
The Wildcat Carnival brought our Altamont elementary students together for an exciting day of hands-on exploration and scientific discovery! Designed to spark curiosity and a love for STEM, the interactive science stations gave students a front-row seat to the wonders of chemistry and physics.

The event featured two major highlights that captured the imagination of our young scientists:

• Elephant's Toothpaste: A crowd-favorite demonstration where students witnessed a rapid, foaming exothermic reaction, illustrating the concepts of chemical energy and heat release in a spectacular display.

• Oobleck Exploration: A dynamic sensory station where students interacted with a fascinating non-Newtonian fluid. By pushing, pulling, and pouring the mixture, they explored how some materials defy standard laws of physics by acting as both a solid and a liquid.

The event highlighted impressive curiosity, critical thinking, and a joy for learning from every participant. Thank you to the families, volunteers, and supporters who helped create an encouraging, high-energy atmosphere that made the day a memorable celebration of student discovery!

description:
Our Foil Boat Competition brought participants together to test their creativity and engineering skills using one simple material: aluminum foil. Each participant designed and built a foil boat, then put it to the test to see how many pennies their boat could hold before sinking.

The event provided a fun, hands-on way to explore STEM concepts, especially the science of buoyancy, stability, and design. Participants learned how small changes in structure can make a big difference—while enjoying some friendly competition.

description:
At Pedrozzi CONNECT Youth, participants joined our Egg Drop Competition and tested their creativity and engineering skills by designing protective containers for raw eggs. 

The event provided a fun, hands-on way to explore STEM concepts, especially the science of impact forces, shock absorption, and design. Participants learned how small changes in structure can make a big difference—while enjoying some friendly competition.
